Engineering Quality Manager, CPU
Arm
Austin, TX
Job ID
2026-19684 Date posted
28/10/2026 Location
Austin, Texas Category

Interested in working with some of the world's most advanced processor technologies and helping make them even better?
We are looking for an Engineering Quality Manager
to join our Central Engineering Quality and Compliance team and work closely with Arm's CPU teams to improve product quality and how we develop, deliver and maintain our IP.
This role covers the CPU development lifecycle, from requirements and design to verification, release and long-term maintenance. It involves working directly with engineers, reviewing existing practices, using data to identify problems and helping teams find better ways of working.
We value curiosity, technical understanding and people who enjoy solving complex problems, asking questions and learning new things. There are opportunities to work across different teams, explore new methods and tools, and contribute your own ideas.
What You'll Do
Provide independent quality oversight for CPU product development and readiness, working with engineering teams to identify risks, review evidence and support decisions throughout the product lifecycle.
Lead quality circles and problem-solving activities, contributing to engineering review boards, defect investigations, root cause analysis and corrective actions. Support urgent customer issues and errata resolution, working with teams to assess impact and resolve issues.
Improve verification effectiveness and engineering quality, introducing practical tools and helping teams strengthen requirements, design and verification practices to prevent problems and detect defects earlier.
Use quality data to identify problems and trends, analyzing errata, quality metrics and customer feedback to understand recurring issues and areas requiring attention.
Find ways to simplify development activities, reduce unnecessary work and share effective methods and lessons learned across Arm.
What We're Looking For
Experience in semiconductor development, verification or engineering quality, with an understanding of RTL/VLSI design, defect management or complex IP development.
Good analytical and problem-solving skills, including root cause analysis, risk identification and the ability to use engineering data to support decisions.
Curiosity about how engineering processes work and an interest in finding ways to improve them.
Good communication skills, with the confidence to challenge experienced engineers constructively, collaborate across teams and respond quickly when priorities change.
Nice to Have
Experience in any of the following areas would be valuable, but is not essential:
CPU architecture, semiconductor productization or hardware/software integration.
Engineering standards, Quality Management Systems, Functional Safety, Automotive Quality or Cybersecurity.
Engineering quality metrics, data analytics, AI or automation tools.
We welcome candidates from different engineering backgrounds. Experience in every area listed above is not required.

$249,900-$338,100 per year

Head of Business Line Operations - Tactical Effects
Anduril Industries
Costa Mesa, California, United States
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
ABOUT THE TEAM
The Tactical Recon and Strike (TRS) team at Anduril develops aerial small drones (Group 1-3) and all equipment to test, deploy and operate. The team is responsible for taking products like Ghost, Bolt, Anvil, and Altius from paper sketches to operational systems. The Tactical Effects Team is a cornerstone business line of the TRS group that is going through tremendous growth. We work in close coordination with specialist teams to solve some of the hardest problems facing our customers. The TRS Operations team is a small but mighty team of business generalists who ‘solve for scale’ the specific business problems that hamper efficiency or productivity. One project may have you solving staffing inefficiencies across engineering teams, while another project may have you working across manufacturing, supply chain, and quality teams to help address capacity or production challenges. We are looking for the Head of Operations to support our Ghost and Precision Engagement Systems business lines, based in Costa Mesa, CA.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
Own all aspects of business operations and infrastructure, ensuring business development, engineering, and production teams have what they need when they need it to execute
Serve as the General Manager’s chief strategist to balance resource and execution risk against our massive growth plans, regularly monitoring financials to help guide us toward our profitability targets
Translate growth signals into demand across all operational infrastructure including staffing, real estate, test ranges, classified infrastructure, and production and collaborate with cross-functional partners across Anduril to deliver
Own the business line’s governance structure from business reviews to annual planning and employee onboarding to all hands, developing and evolving information pathways as the organization scales
Collaborate closely with division leadership to evolve the organizational structure and define and implement strong hiring, onboarding, and execution standards for key functions so we maintain a culture of “doing things differently”
Execute on special projects, evolve internal processes, spearhead the stand up of new functions, and lead M&A efforts as needed
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
You have 5-7+ years of varied experience in an operating role at a high-growth technology company, starting a venture, or in finance or consulting
You love solving complex, ambiguous, cross-functional problems in a people-centric way
You’re both high ownership and low ego, approaching everything with strong outcome orientation and high humility
You’re highly detail oriented and data-driven
You’re discerning and an incredibly fast learner
You’re tactical and enjoy getting into the details.
US Salary Range
$183,000—$243,000 USD
The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:
Benefits
At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.
Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams
Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.
To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:
No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
Please always verify communications:
Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.
Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.
Data Privacy
To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.
By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

Operations Director- Manufacturing
Jabil
Florence, KY
Jabil, Inc. is seeking a proven Operations Director to lead site operations and drive excellence across Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, and People. With oversight of Manufacturing, Quality, Safety, Test, Engineering, and Facilities, this leader will set operational strategy, develop high-performing teams, and ensure the organization has the capability and capacity to meet evolving customer demand. The Operations Director will also serve as a senior partner to Business Unit leadership and customers, driving continuous improvement and delivering sustainable operational results in a complex, high-mix, high-volume manufacturing environment.
What will you do?
Leadership and Organization
Lead the Operations Manager and all functional managers as direct reports, with a single point of accountability for Site performance across all shifts (24/7 operations).
Design and adjust the Site organization to support growth, ramps, and long-term site stability.
Hire, develop, and retain senior leaders. Work with Talent Acquisition on capability requirements and selection criteria for management roles.
Coach leaders on decision-making, performance management, and accountability.
Align manufacturing and the functions on shared priorities, and resolve conflicts between them.
Talent Development and Succession
Own succession planning and bench strength for critical leadership roles across the Site.
Track turnover, engagement, and organizational health, and put retention and development plans in place.
Make sure leadership development, training, and standard work are in place and working.
Build a culture of ownership, accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
Performance Management and Execution
Set site goals tied to Business Unit and Sr Leadership and cascade them through the organization.
Own the Site operating system: KPIs, dashboards, and tiered accountability reviews from the floor to site leadership.
Give timely, direct feedback to leaders based on performance data and what you see on the floor.
Make sure performance evaluations across the organization are accurate, fair, and on time.
Lead the site through ramps, escalations, and disruptions while keeping focus and discipline.
Business Strategy and Customer Alignment
Turn corporate and Business Unit strategy into executable site plans.
Align manufacturing, test, and support capacity with customer requirements, demand forecasts, and financial targets.
Represent the Site with customers in business reviews, audits, and escalations.
Update Business Unit and senior leadership regularly on performance, risks, and improvement initiatives.
Financial and Resource Management
Own the Site cost drivers (labor, overhead, and capital) and drive cost reduction and productivity improvements.
Approve and manage headcount plans, capacity models, and capital investments with Finance.
Make sure corrective actions are in place and tracked when cost, productivity, or delivery targets are missed.
Technical and Operational Excellence
Drive continuous improvement through data analysis, KPI management, and structured problem-solving (QRQC, RCA, Kaizen).
Make sure standard work, procedures, and work instructions are effective, current, and followed in every function.
Work with Engineering, Quality, and Test to improve process capability, yield, and customer satisfaction.
Promote best practices and share learnings with other Jabil sites.
Own Site compliance with Jabil policies, including Safety, Quality, Security, and Confidentiality, as well as regulatory and customer audits.
Set the tone for a strong safety culture and make sure all health and safety requirements are followed.
How will you get here?
Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience. Advanced degree preferred.
8-15 years of manufacturing or operations experience, including at least 7 years in a senior leadership role managing managers and multiple functions.
Hands-on leader who leads from the front and drives culture and change.
Experience in a complex, matrixed, fast-paced manufacturing environment (EMS preferred), including site ramps or large-scale growth.
Ability to influence customers, executives, and peers at all levels.
Strong safety mindset and a record of building a safety culture.
Working knowledge of operational metrics, labor and capacity planning, financial management, and continuous improvement tools.
Proficiency with Workday, SAP (ERP/MES), and Microsoft Office.
Willingness to be on the floor and flex across shifts as the business requires.

Casting Engineering Supervisor
Ford Motor Company
Dearborn, MI
We made history and now we work to transform the future – for our customers, our communities and our families. You'll see your work on the road every day, helping people move freely and pursue their dreams. At Ford, you can build more than vehicles. Come build what matters.
As part of our Manufacturing
team, you’ll help build the world-class, state-of-the-art smart vehicles we're known for. In our plants around the world, we’re constantly developing new technologies and processes to further increase our efficiency. You'll get the satisfaction of making great products people use and love.
In this position...
The Casting Manufacturing Engineering Supervisor will have the responsibility to lead and develop a team to ensure the highest quality and most efficient designs and processes are being used, experience leading cross functional teams in fast paced manufacturing environments. The candidate should have knowledge of various casting alloys and processes, including but not limited to gravity, low-pressure, and high pressure die casting. Knowledge of various core making processes and materials will be useful.
What You'll Do...
Drive the New Model Launch of Complex Casting (NMLCC) process, which will provide a framework to enable the cross functional teams to create Program / Component specific plans, for the development and implementation of manufacturing feasible casting designs and processes resulting in parts that can be machined by standard and best practice methods in support of new Powertrain program product launches.
Assess employee competencies and support development and upskilling as necessary. Mentor less experienced employees within and outside of the organization related to Casting Engineering.
Support simultaneous engineering and feasibility engineering studies among product engineering, manufacturing engineering and supplier organizations.
Support quality improvement activities, root cause identification and defect elimination strategies.
Support supplier selection evaluation process through manufacturing assessments and assist Purchasing in the evaluation, development, and selection of suppliers and subcontractors.
Provide support for casting prototype planning, process development and scheduling.
Support on-time quality prototype delivery of new Ford components at internal and external supplier facilities.
Evaluate innovative and disruptive emerging processes and material technologies for potential application to Ford products.
Support Product Engineering in the selection and specification of component materials and test procedures.
Assist Ford manufacturing plants, as required, in resolving significant engineering issues and achieving continuous improvement for both new programs and current production.
Provide technical support, as required, to Purchasing (Component Buyers and Supplier Technical Assistance) involving the resolution of casting related productivity and quality issues and the development of external casting suppliers.
Perform supervisory duties including but not limited to objective and goal development, development discussions and performance reviews.
You'll have...
Bachelor of Science/Engineering; MBA/MS preferred - Chemical/Electrical/Mechanical or Metallurgy/Materials Science.
Min of 10+ years in Manufacturing
Min of 6+ years in Casting.
Ability to demonstrate you can lead a team.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills to present, persuade, and collaborate at all levels of the organization.
Working level knowledge of casting, post processing, and die development processes.
Working level knowledge of core making processes and materials.
Knowledge of the secondary operations associated with castings, including, but not limited to trimming, fettling, deburring, and quality checks.
Knowledge of both iron and aluminum alloys used for castings.
Understanding of MagmaSoft or other casting simulation software results. Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to make decisions in a fast paced, dynamic environment.

Description
In Annapurna Labs we are at the forefront of hardware/software accelerator solutions for not only Amazon Web Services (AWS), but across the industry. The Annapurna AI Systems team owns design, validation, deployment, manufacturing, quality, reliability and fleet operations end to end.
Turning the silicon and systems into serving capacity is a manufacturing problem at a scale and pace the industry has not run before: cards, boards, sleds and servers built into racks across a global manufacturing footprint, then shipped to globally diverse datacenters and converted into capacity customers can launch on.
The Trainium Manufacturing, Quality and Reliability team owns that path end to end, and we looking for candidates interested in diving deep into our manufacturing, scaling and quality processes to support current and future generations of accelerator silicon/systems.
You will be responsible for managing server and rack manufacturing programs across our North America footprint — build plan attainment, rolled-through yield, test cycle time, work-in-process health and on-time shipment to datacenter — at ODM and CM sites.
We are seeking an experienced TPM who is equally comfortable on a factory floor and in a data set. You will reconcile what a partner reports, what the test data says, and what the design actually permits — and then drive the plan that closes the gap. Come join us!
Key job responsibilities
You will own manufacturing programs end to end across our ODM and CM partners: build rate against plan, rolled-through yield, first-pass test cycle time, aged work-in-process, and on-time shipment to datacenter.
You will establish the operating cadence with each partner — weekly build and recovery reviews, clear commitments, and an escalation path into vendor leadership that you are trusted to use.
You will own material readiness, operational support and constraint resolution — critical component supply, mechanical and enclosure quality, and staging capacity at each site. The job is to identify the constraint before it caps the build rate, and to drive the cross-functional plan that clears it.
You will drive manufacturing readiness for new rack platforms, defining entry and exit criteria for each build phase and gating ramp decisions on demonstrated yield and cycle time rather than on schedule pressure.
You will coordinate across Design Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Manufacturing Test, Quality and Reliability, Supply Chain, Global Supplier Management, Logistics and EC2. Manufacturing sits between design intent and deployed capacity.
You will build the reporting layer — define the metrics that describe manufacturing health, automate them where you can, and give senior leadership a clear weekly position on what shipped, what is at risk, what you need and by when.
You will work independently in a dynamic, challenging, and fast-changing organization. We’re changing an industry, and we need individuals who are ready for this challenge and who want to reach beyond what is possible today.
A day in the life
Your day to day responsibilities will include interfacing with our engineering teams, vendors and customers to understand project requirements and facilitate manufacturing output and scaling . You will work directly with vendors and ODM/JDM/CM teams to develop and manufacture your product at scale.
You will review build, yield and ship numbers from each site against plan and determine key bottlenecks and engage the right teams to overcome them. You will lead output and recovery reviews with ODM/CM leadership, pushing back on a commitment you do not believe the line can hold and landing on a number you can both defend. You will coordinate with vendor and Amazon supply chain teams to align materials with your build plans. You will write daily/weekly reports as necessary to inform leadership on the current state and key challenges.

Our team is dedicated to supporting new members. We have a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge-sharing and mentorship. We care about your career growth and strive to assign projects that help our team members develop your engineering expertise so you feel empowered to take on more complex tasks in the future. Head of Manufacturing
Powertown
Boston, Massachusetts
Overview
We need someone who has taken hardware from a successful first unit to repeatable, high-volume manufacturing, and who wants to build that function from scratch. You'll own everything between "the engineering team built one that works" and "we can build hundreds of these reliably, on schedule, at cost."
What You'll Do
Own the transition from prototype builds to scaled Powerblock production, standing up the manufacturing function from the ground up
Develop equipment, fixtures, and processes for early-stage builds and design them to scale into high-volume production
Determine and procure manufacturing equipment, working with integrators on semi-automated through fully automated systems as volume justifies it
Manage suppliers through specification, design, buyoff, and installation of manufacturing equipment
Provide DFM input back to the hardware team to improve yield and manufacturability as the Powerblock design matures
Create manufacturing instructions and documentation to train the technicians who'll build production units
Set the cost, quality, and throughput targets that let us hit our per-unit hardware cost goals at scale
What You'll Bring
5+ years hands-on as a Mechanical, Manufacturing, or Design Engineer on mechanical or electromechanical systems, ideally with time spent taking a product from prototype to volume production
2D CAD for line design (AutoCAD) and 3D CAD for equipment, fixturing, and tooling (SolidWorks or CATIA)
Experience with conveyance, workstation design, robotic systems, adhesive dispensing, DC fastening tools, or automated functional test
GD&T and system stack-up analysis
Experience writing technical specifications for automated manufacturing equipment
DFM and DFA experience, and comfort giving that input directly to a hardware design team
Comfort operating with almost no existing infrastructure. You're building the manufacturing function, not stepping into one.
Nice to Have
Background in battery, energy storage, or power electronics hardware
Experience standing up a manufacturing line at an early-stage hardware startup
Familiarity with domestic content and manufacturing tax accounting
